identity.title: MuonSSM: Orthogonalizing State Space Models for Sequence Modeling

problem.claim: Develop stable, scalable long-sequence modeling with efficient SSMs.

gap.claim: Existing SSMs are reported to experience instability and memory degradation over long horizons, associated with poorly conditioned first-order updates and unbalanced update geometry.

contributions.claim: Introduces MuonSSM, which conditions the geometry of memory updates rather than the recurrent transition matrix.
Adds a momentum pathway and lightweight Newton–Schulz transformation on low-rank input injections, while preserving parallel-scan complexity.
Provides theoretical results on gradient propagation, spectral amplification, and long-horizon memory representations.

stated_novelty.claim: The authors distinguish MuonSSM by explicitly geometrically conditioning memory updates instead of conditioning the recurrent transition matrix.

author_reported_evidence.claim: The authors report that theory shows improved gradient propagation, reduced spectral amplification, and richer long-horizon memory representations.
Across language, vision, and time-series benchmarks, the authors report consistent gains in accuracy, robustness, and long-context performance when MuonSSM is integrated into diverse SSM backbones.

narrative_sequence.summary: SSMs are presented as efficient linear-time alternatives to attention for long sequences.
The abstract identifies instability and memory degradation over extended horizons, linked to update conditioning and geometry.
MuonSSM conditions memory-update geometry using momentum and a low-rank Newton–Schulz transformation while retaining parallel scans.
Theory and cross-domain benchmarks are reported to support improved propagation, memory behavior, robustness, and long-context performance.
The authors frame update geometry conditioning as a principled route to stable, scalable sequence modeling.

source_observation.claim: The abstract connects a specific failure mode—long-horizon instability and memory degradation—to update geometry, then aligns the proposed mechanism and reported evidence with that diagnosis.

lessons.interpretation: A focused problem–mechanism–evidence chain can make a technical contribution easier to assess.
lessons.application: Frame a model paper by naming the failure mode, identifying the targeted structural cause, and reporting evidence that directly tests the corresponding behavior.
lessons.exception: This framing is unsuitable when the claimed cause is only speculative or when available evaluations do not measure the targeted behavior.

unknowns: The abstract gives no benchmark names, dataset sizes, numerical gains, baselines, or ablations.
The conditions and formal assumptions behind the theoretical claims are unspecified.
The abstract does not detail what robustness measures or long-context settings were used.
